question.text: While returning home from a movie theatre, Ahmed Bouchikhi was misidentified and killed by members of this Israeli intelligence agency in Operation Wrath of God.
question.clue: This agency undertook an extrajudicial operation which captured and led to the execution of Adolf Eichmann after he was discovered hiding in Argentina.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about prominent terrorist groups.
swap.text: This group, led by Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, was responsible for the attacks in November 2015 on Paris that killed 130 people.
swap.clue: Brett McGurk is the American special envoy to a coalition against this group.

question.text: This Islamic political organization was suppressed during Mubarak's time in office, but formed the Freedom and Justice Party to contest elections after Mubarak's resignation.
question.answerHtml: Muslim Brotherhood (accept The Society of the Muslim Brothers)
question.clue: Its first meeting place was created in Ismailia by its founder Hassan al-Bannah ("HAH-sen al-buh-NAH").

swap.leadin: The secret Protocol of Sevres was a plan for Great Britain and France to "mediate" this event, in which they would take over the waterway in question.
swap.text: Name this 1956 conflict in which Israel invaded Egypt in response to Gamal Abdel Nasser's nationalization of the namesake canal near the Sinai Peninsula.
swap.clue: This conflict was the center of discussions at the Protocol of Sevres after which Charles Keightley initiated Operation Musketeer.

question.leadin: This war opened with a pre-emptive strike on one country's air force called Operation Focus.
question.text: Name this short 1967 conflict in which Egypt, Syria, and Jordan lost the Sinai, West Bank, Gaza, and the Golan Heights. UN Resolution 242 was passed after this war.
question.answerHtml: Six-Day war [or June War or Third Arab-Israeli War; prompt on Arab-Israeli War]
question.clue: This war began with the airstrike Operation Focus after the losing side closed the Straits of Tiran.

swap.text: The Makurian king Kyriakos later invaded Egypt to free a Christian patriarch imprisoned by this caliphate. This caliphate was founded by Muawiyah I and ruled from Damascus until its fall in the Abbasid Revolution.
swap.clue: Its forces under Marwan II lost the Battle of the Zab, and Charles Martel defeated Moorish forces under this dynasty at the Battle of Tours.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Turkish migration from Central Asia.
question.text: This second sultan of the Seljuqs fought a war against the Fatimids in Syria. He defeated the Byzantine army at the Battle of Manzikert, where he captured the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV.
question.answerHtml: Alp Arslan [accept Muhammad bin Dawud Chaghri , prompt on Heroic Lion ]
question.clue: According to Edward Gibbon, this man died when he waved his bodyguards away and tried to shoot an assassin with his own bow.

swap.text: At first, some suspected the explosion to have been the result of a terrorist attack by this Shiite terrorist group. This terrorist group is led by Hassan Nasrallah, and was heavily backed by Iranian commander Qassem Soleimani.
swap.clue: Led by Hassan Nasrallah, and given major funding by Iran, this group's 2006 kidnapping of Israeli soldiers sparked a brief war between Israel and the country which it controls large parts of.

question.text: One major goal of the Ottoman government in the nineteenth century was the settlement of this mostly nomadic people in Eastern Anatolia. They briefly formed an independent principality under 'Ubaydallah in 1880 and came into bloody conflict with Armenian farmers.
question.clue: This group ruled the ephemeral Soviet satellite state called the Republic of Mahabad, and later, their namesake Workers Party was founded by Abdullah Ocalan .

swap.leadin: This successor of al-Mahdi was advised by his Barmakid vizier Yahya, and with his son al-Ma'mun established the Hosue of Wisdom.
swap.text: Identify this Islamic ruler, the subject of much of the Meadows of Gold, who presided over a high point of culture and civilization during the eighth century.
swap.answerHtml: Harun al-Rashid [or the Upright; or the Just; or the Rightly Guided; accept Aaron]
swap.clue: He even laid the groundwork for civil war by dividing the succession between his sons al-Amin and al-Ma'mun.

question.leadin: His followers called themselves "al-Muwahhidun," which translates roughly as "Unitarians," and he is the author of the Kitab al-tawhid.
question.text: Identify this man who first took a stand against innovation in his religion in 1736.
question.clue: In his hometown of Uyaynah, he gained the favor of a ruler named Uthman, whom he directed to begin a campaign of iconoclasm, destroying the domes on the gravesites of Muhammad's companion.

swap.text: The controversial April Fool's Day episode "Terrance and Phillip in Not Without My Anus" sees the title duo save Canada by using flatulence to kill this world leader. [10] In real life, this man was captured in Operation Red Dawn and executed in 2006. His sons Uday and Qusay were killed, not by flatulence but with bullets, in 2003.
swap.clue: This leader was ultimately captured in Operation Red Dawn and then interrogated by FBI Agent George Piro.

question.text: The Banu Musa brothers worked alongside this scholar, who translated the Roman cartography treatise Geography into Arabic. Another treatise by this scholar introduced Indian numerals to the Arabic world.

swap.leadin: Name these dynasties of world history which existed in 1000 A.D.
swap.text: This dynasty was just getting going, after Said ibn Husayn of northern Syria founded it and its fourth ruler Moizz moved the capital to Cairo. It's named for a daughter of the prophet Muhammad.
swap.clue: Turkish general al-Basasiri handed control of Baghdad to this caliphate, but he was later driven out by Seljuks, and the Byzantines ended up driving it out of Sicily.

question.text: After Gemayel's assassination, the IDF gave Phalangist militias access to a refugee camp and a Shia neighborhood in Beirut, resulting in this massacre that forced Ariel Sharon ("sha-ROHN") to resign as defense minister.
question.clue: Elie Hobeika's forces were able to carry on slaughtering people through the night thanks to flares fired from a third party, which led the Kahan Commission to declare the sitting Defense Minister "personally responsible."

swap.text: Ten years prior, Christians in this city were massacred by Muslims during an event known as The Events. Between 2012 and 2016, sites in this city such as its Citadel and nine historic gates were damaged by artillery fire.
swap.clue: A rebuilt version of the Ayyubid Palace of Glory is contained within a defensive structure used by Seleucus Nicator, this massive Citadel of this city, outside of which Tamerlane built a tower of 20,000 skulls after taking it from the Mamluks.

question.text: The first Umayyad, Abu Sufyan, was a member of this tribe, which controlled Mecca during the time of Muhammad. Divisions of this tribe included the Banu Hashim.
question.answerHtml: Quraysh [or Kuraish or Koreish or Quresh or Qurrish or Qurish or Qirsh or Qureshi or Coreish]
question.clue: Muhammad's Hashemites were one of 10 clans in this ruling tribe of Mecca. The Umayyads and Rashiduns traced their lineage to other clans in this group of peoples.

swap.leadin: This commander originally fought against and defeated Muhammed at the Battle of Uhud, but after his conversion led the Muslims to victory at Mu'Tah and Taif.
swap.text: Identify this brilliant Arab General, known as "The Sword of Allah," who destroyed the Sassanid empire in Mesopotamia, ended the Riddah wars, conquered most of Syria, and did it all while being spectacularly outnumbered in almost every battle.
swap.clue: This man was officially dismissed from his command for bestowing a large sum of money on the poet Ash'as for a poem praising his deeds.

question.text: 'Arib claimed to have been born into this family of Iranian nobles, who were originally a group of Buddhist leaders in Balkh. Under the Abbasids, this family became a dynasty of viziers, starting with its member Khalid.
question.clue: Harun also destroyed the power of this family after one of its members impregnated his sister Abassa. This family patronized scholars such as Geber and was influential during the early years of the caliphate.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Suez Crisis.
swap.text: This was the code name for the Anglo-French invasion plan. It quickly followed Israel's invasion of the Sinai, which was known as Operation Kadesh.
